newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia expects to hit 1997 grain target - Itar-Tass.
newsitem.headline: Russia expects to hit 1997 grain target - Itar-Tass.

text.p: Russia is on course to hit its grain production target of 70 million tonnes in 1997, unnamed sources in the Agriculture Ministry were quoted by Itar-Tass news agency as saying on Wednesday.
Russia's net grain harvest recovered to 69.3 million tonnes in 1996, up from 63.4 million in 1995, but was still one of the worst crops during the last three decades.
The winter grain crop was in good condition, with little winter-kill expected, and the spring sowing campaign was running well ahead of year-ago levels, ministry sources were quoted as saying.
Some Russian research institutes have raised doubts over whether the ministry's official net grain output target of 70 million tonnes could be reached.
Estimates of the 1997 net grain output forecasts by various research bodies during the last month have ranged from just 60.0 to 63.0 million tonnes.
Western agriculture analysts have said it is too early to forecast.
But they agreed that winter kill losses this year would fall below average levels and that the weather forecasts for the summer were generally favourable for the harvest.
However, they said a smaller area was sown to grains during the winter crop sowing campaign last autumn.
